draft.title: Responses at different scales
card: Sustainability problems such as climate change cross borders and affect every level of society. Responses are needed at several scales, and each scale can do things the others cannot.
International
Countries agree on shared goals, such as the Paris Agreement on cutting emissions. They cannot force a country to act, so the goals depend on each country following through.
National
A government can make laws, set targets and fund projects across a whole country. Examples are a carbon price, a ban on single-use plastic bags or support for renewable energy.
Local and personal
Businesses can change how they make and sell goods. Communities can run local projects such as tree planting. Individuals can change what they buy, use and throw away.
draft.remember: Sustainability needs action at many scales, and each scale can do things the others cannot.

a.q: Why does a global problem such as climate change need responses at more than one scale?
opts: Each scale can do things that the others cannot
Action at one scale makes action at others unnecessary
Only international agreements can change what people do
Individuals and businesses have no effect on emissions
a.why: Each scale has its own strengths: agreements set shared goals, governments make laws, and businesses, communities and individuals change daily practice. It is wrong to say one scale replaces the others, because each depends on the rest.
a.clue: Think about what a law can do that one household cannot, and the reverse.

b.q: The council in a coastal town in New South Wales runs a beach dune planting program, and local residents volunteer to plant. Which scale of response is this?
opts: Community, through local action by residents
International, through a shared agreement
National, through a law set by the federal government
Individual, because each volunteer acts alone
b.why: The program is run locally and involves residents working together on a shared project, so it is a community response. It is not individual, because the action is organised as a group, even though each volunteer is a person.
b.clue: Who organises the action, and how many people work on it together?

a.best: Each scale can do things that the others cannot

b.best: Community, through local action by residents

problems.detail: The program is run by the council, which is local government, but the card never mentions local councils. It only links government to the national scale. The keyed answer credits the action to residents as a community, so a careful student may be unsure how to place a council-run program. Saying a community group runs it, or mentioning local government on the card, would remove the doubt.

check.summary: The card is accurate and both questions have one clear right answer. The only minor issue is that question b names a council as the organiser, and the card never covers local government.

problems.detail: A ban on single-use plastic bags is given as a national-scale example. In Australia these bans were made by state and territory governments, not the federal government. NSW students could wrongly take this as a federal law. Either name it as a state law or use an example that is national in Australia.

The distractors are implausible for Year 12 HSC students ('Individuals and businesses have no effect on emissions', 'Action at one scale makes action at others unnecessary'). The right option also repeats the card's wording almost exactly, so a student can pick it without understanding the idea.
